we have developed a breast cancer predictor using gene expression data from the peripheral blood of mice.

developing a blood-based predictor for human breast cancer based on the transcriptome data from a transgenic mouse model of breast tumors.

the results of this work are encouraging and suggest that the use of animal models for the development of blood-based diagnostics is a feasible approach, but further studies in larger cohorts are needed to confirm the results and validate the model.

it is feasible to use an animal model to identify a blood-based predictor for a human disease.
the use of a model system to reduce confounders and identify a core biological response is an effective strategy for generating a diagnostic predictor.
a mouse model of a human disease, when combined with appropriate statistical modeling, can be a useful starting point for the discovery of a diagnostic for that disease.
